transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling a lot with my eating lately. It feels like once I start eating after my night shifts, I just can't stop or control how much I'm eating, and it's really starting to worry me.
Can you describe a typical episode where you feel like you've lost control over your eating, and does this happen only after your night shifts or at other times as well?

During an episode, I’ll stand in the kitchen or breakroom and just shovel down tons of food—like sandwiches, pizza, and cookies—eating so fast I barely taste it, feeling like a switch flipped in my brain and I literally can't stop. It mostly happens after my night shifts, but it also occurs when I'm up late at home avoiding my design projects, even when I'm not actually hungry.
After one of these episodes of eating, do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or upset about what you've eaten or how much you've eaten?

Yes, I feel incredibly ashamed, disgusted, and weak afterward. I usually just sit there staring at the empty wrappers, blaming myself for gaining weight and not getting my life together. Those feelings of guilt are so overwhelming that they can completely ruin my entire morning or day.

Can you estimate how often these episodes of losing control over eating happen in a given week, and do you ever engage in any behaviors to compensate for the binge eating, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or excessive exercise?

These episodes happen at least once a week, and often more, usually after my night shifts or when I'm staying up late. I don't throw up or use laxatives to make up for it. In fact, instead of exercising more, I've actually been skipping my usual running and basketball club because I feel too sluggish and ashamed.
Can you tell me more about how your eating patterns and feelings of loss of control are related to your night shifts and stress, and are there any other factors that seem to trigger these episodes?

My job as a night-shift cleaner leaves me alone for long stretches with irregular breaks, making it easy to graze on vending machines and leftover catered food in the offices to stay awake. I also get incredibly stressed and frustrated because my design portfolio has stalled and I'm procrastinating on my schoolwork. When I feel stuck or anxious about my future, I end up eating to cope with those feelings, even when I'm not actually hungry.

Can you describe how your eating habits and feelings of control change when you're not working night shifts and are engaged in activities you enjoy, like working on your design portfolio or playing basketball?

Honestly, I haven't been able to do those activities much lately. When my design projects stall or I procrastinate, it actually triggers my urge to eat to cope with the frustration. I've also stopped playing basketball and running with my club because I feel too sluggish, bloated, and ashamed after my eating episodes, so I've lost those positive outlets.
Have you ever experienced a period of at least three months where you didn't have these episodes of binge eating, or has this pattern of eating been relatively consistent over time?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that. This pattern has been really consistent for about fourteen months now, ever since I started working more night shifts. I haven't gone more than a week or two without an episode, let alone three months.

Can you confirm if your binge eating episodes occur, on average, at least once a week for the past three months, and if there's any significant variation in the frequency or severity of these episodes over time?

Yes, I can confirm that. For the last several months, it has happened at least once a week, and often even more than that. The pattern has stayed really steady for about fourteen months now, with the frequency mostly tied to how stressed I am with my night shifts and school.

You've mentioned not using laxatives or vomiting to compensate, but have you ever engaged in any other forms of purging or compensatory behaviors, such as fasting or strict dieting, after these binge eating episodes?
No, I don't do any fasting or strict dieting to make up for it. Honestly, I usually just feel too sluggish and ashamed to do much of anything at all after those nights.
